title: Pointed profinite etale limit and its Cech component coordinates
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty connected quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and let $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Put $\Pi=\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X,x)$ with its profinite topology [def-galois-fibre-functor]. A pointed connected finite etale Galois cover means a finite etale $X$-scheme $Y$, a point $y\in Y_x$, and a connected total space, with its $X$-automorphism group acting simply transitively on $Y_x$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. Let $T$ be the inverse limit over a small cofinal system of these pointed covers and pointed transition maps, taken in schemes over $X$. This limit exists, is connected, and its projection $v:T\to X$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], faithfully flat (flat and surjective on spectra) [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism] and weakly etale [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism]; the singleton $\{v\}$ is a covering in $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The compatible points define $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ above $x$.

For every finite etale $X$-scheme $Y$ there is a canonical splitting
$$T\times_XY\simeq\coprod_{s\in Y_x}T,$$
natural in $Y$, whose section indexed by $s$ takes $t$ to $s$. Write $T\times\Pi^q=\varprojlim_N\coprod_{(\Pi/N)^q}T$, for open normal subgroups $N\subseteq\Pi$. There are compatible Cech identifications
$$T^{q+1}_{/X}\simeq T\times\Pi^q\quad(q\geq0),\qquad \pi_0(T^{q+1}_{/X})\simeq\Pi^q,$$
where the component space has its quotient topology. These coordinates have the group-nerve faces: consecutive labels $g,h$ compose to $gh$. For a right torsor with a chosen section over $T$, the Cech cocycle equation is $c(z,gh)=c(z,g)c(z\cdot g,h)$, where $z\cdot g$ denotes the second vertex with first vertex $z$ and label $g$, and coefficient sections are pulled back to the triple overlap. When the transition element depends only on the group label, this specializes to $c(gh)=c(g)c(h)$. They are normalized by the finite fibre functor's left monodromy action. More explicitly, for $U\subseteq\Pi$ open, on $T\times_XT$ the canonical sections of the split cover with fibre $\Pi/U$ obey $\mathrm{pr}_2^*s=\mathrm{pr}_1^*(g s)$ at label $g$. The construction is natural for pointed scheme morphisms, with the induced homomorphism on fundamental groups acting on these labels. The inverse limits and coproducts use compatible universes.

proof.text: Use exists_pointedGaloisLimitGeometry to obtain the equivalence with open normal subgroups, its pointed equivariant labels, and the already constructed UniversalCover geometry. Form PointedCosetSystem using the inverse labels and PointedCosetLimit using the whiskered existing cone in schemes over X. Initial whiskering gives its universal property; the supplied marked point gives all point equations.

Apply exists_pointedLimitSplitting to this supplied limit. The section_point and existing eq_toObj uniqueness identify every sectionMap with UniversalCover.toObj. Testing every toObj identifies its normalized deck maps with rightDeck. Its coproduct cofan proves the specified finiteSplitMap is an isomorphism, and its section_deck, deck_mul and deck_one give the action equations.

Apply exists_coordinates to the supplied splitting. Compare its finiteLabelDiagram limit cone with the actual profinite-product limit supplied by profinite_scheme_product_components, using the unique isomorphism between limit cones. Constant sections agree after all finite quotient legs, hence agree by limit uniqueness. Transport the first vertex, cumulative vertices and all-simplex equations through this comparison. Transport the component homeomorphism of the actual product along the resulting scheme isomorphism, obtaining the stipulated component-label formula. No automorphism-group profiniteness theorem is needed because the input G is already a ProfiniteGrp.

For naturality, the base-change fibre isomorphism and fundamentalGroupMap_smul make the right deck maps commute with UniversalCover.map, as checked against every toObj. For two maps over X to a finite etale cover, equality after every constant-label section implies equality: pull back the open diagonal along their pair. The product space homeomorphism puts every point on a constant-label section, so this open immersion is surjective and hence an isomorphism. Apply this detection to each finite-cover section of every Cech vertex. Cumulative products commute with the induced group homomorphism. Wide-pullback extensionality proves the naturality equality for arbitrary supplied coordinates.

Pull the right-torsor transition equation along each of the three edges, use the vertex identities and naturality, combine the two right actions by associativity, and cancel the common section using freeness. Substitute the label-only formula and evaluate at any point of the nonempty base for its specialization. Identity and composition of pointed limit maps follow from uniqueness of maps from a connected scheme to each finite etale cover with a fixed marked value, then limit extensionality.
